Hi Sam — great to meet you today. Added Monica and Ben from our implementation and API-seed teams; they'll own the steps below. High-level answers and the proposed plan: 

1) Service accounts: we recommend two service accounts for separation of duty — one for ingestion (gridlabs-ingest) and one for runtime/model calls (gridlabs-runtime). This lets you apply tighter KMS and network rules to ingestion pipelines.

2) Project naming: pattern gridlabs-<env> is fine. Avoid underscores; max length is 32 chars on our side.

3) API keys: we can seed long-lived API keys for admin users within 48 business hours after we confirm the admin roster. We will also provide ephemeral keys for CI testing if you prefer (good for short-lived test runners).

4) Invite cadence: proposed sequence below (Monica will confirm):
   - Day 0: create two admin users (email invites + org-admin role)
   - Day 1: seed 2 service accounts and provision initial API keys
   - Day 2: invite 5 read-only and 2 dev users

Action items for GridLabs (please reply):
- Confirm admin emails (for initial two admins)
- Confirm whether you want ephemeral keys for CI or just long-lived seeds
- Any special compliance gating (e.g., IP allowlist) we should pre-configure?

Thanks — Monica will follow up with the invite schedule and the API-seed playbook.

— Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Hi Sam — following up with an operational playbook draft. Keeping it lightweight so your infra can start testing this week.

Playbook (high level):
- Day 0 (kickoff): Create org entry in Redwood Console: name "GridLabs", region us-west1. Set org-level SSO = off for now.
- Admins: create two admin accounts and assign role = org-admin. Confirmed: admin emails needed by EOD.
- Service accounts: we will create gridlabs-ingest@redwood-sa and gridlabs-runtime@redwood-sa. Each service account will have a single API key stored in your encrypted secrets bucket. Keys will be marked as 'rotation: manual' by default.
- API key seeding: Ben will run the seed script to create keys in the staging project and hand off the key values via the secure link in Redwood Drive (link below).
- Invite cadence: we'll send the admin invites first, wait for acceptance, then seed keys the next day, then bulk invite dev/read-only users the following day.

Optional (recommended):
- Enable IP allowlist for ingestion service account if GridLabs has a stable set of egress IPs.
- If you want CI ephemeral keys, we'll create a token issuer that mints 1-hour tokens for your CI runners. This requires an additional integration and a 1-week lead time.

Please confirm the admin emails and whether to proceed with ephemeral CI tokens. If you have a preferred naming convention for secrets stores, note it here.

Secure handoff links: https://redwood-drive.example.com/teams/onboarding/GridLabs/kickoff-notes

— Monica Patel
Implementation Lead | Redwood Inference
